slides.title: A small screen has a clear owner map
slides.lead: 320 × 240 pixels; origin at top-left; y increases downward.
points: Firmware owns y=0…45 and y=222…239
Your page body is y=46…221: 176 pixels high
The emulator marks the body boundary; its drawing is illustrative
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Open a named page
slides.lead: Display.open connects and creates or reuses a page.
points: Reusing METER avoids consuming another slot
The board supports three custom pages plus HOST
If slots are full, reuse a name or reset the board
slides.code:
import robotos_edge as rk
d = rk.Display.open(args.port, name="METER")
src = imu_source(args, d.session)
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Queue operations, then flush
slides.lead: Drawing calls queue operations on the host.
points: clear, text and fill_rect describe work for the board
flush sends queued operations and polls board events
It splits/paces batches; it is not an atomic double-buffered frame swap
slides.code:
d.clear()
d.text(10, 56, "Lab 9.3 |a| meter", rk.Color.WHITE)
d.fill_rect(10, 110, 120, 30, rk.Color.GREEN)
d.flush()
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Understand rectangle arguments
slides.lead: x and y locate the top-left; w and h are sizes.
points: fill_rect paints an area; rect draws its border
circle uses center x,y and radius; line uses endpoints
The text font uses 8 × 16 pixel cells
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: RGB565 packs colour into 16 bits
slides.lead: Red: 5 bits · Green: 6 bits · Blue: 5 bits
points: Bit shifts discard low-order RGB888 bits
Two nearby RGB888 values may become the same RGB565 colour
The browser preview cannot reproduce the physical panel’s gamma
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: A full frame has a real cost
points: At 10 full frames/s: 1,536,000 pixel bytes/s before overhead
A filled rectangle can be sent as a compact drawing operation
Pixel area and USB command bytes are different budgets
slides.notes: Use the exact byte count; do not imply the SDK always sends full-frame bitmaps.

slides.title: Respect the command budget
slides.lead: The inspected SDK batches at most 32 operations and about 1 KB per message.
points: flush paces batches and can wait for command acknowledgements
More operations can mean more latency even with tiny payloads
The lesson’s ~10 updates/s line demo is a reported measurement, not a guarantee
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Map magnitude to a clipped width
slides.lead: A_MAX=30 m/s² maps to BAR_W=300 pixels.
points: Divide by the maximum to form a fraction
Clip to [0,1] to stay inside the bar
Multiply by width, then int truncates to an integer pixel
slides.code:
width = int(min(max(s.a_mag / A_MAX, 0.0), 1.0) * BAR_W)
color = rk.Color.GREEN if s.a_mag < 15 else rk.Color.YELLOW if s.a_mag < 22 else rk.Color.RED
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Why clearing can flicker
slides.lead: The panel may refresh between erase and redraw.
points: Draw titles, frames and scale once
Keep the previous width and colour as state
Update changed regions; do not clear the whole page each frame
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Growing and shrinking need different rectangles
slides.lead: A 200 → 150 px bar needs a 50 × 30 px erase.
points: Grow: paint the new segment
Shrink: erase the extra segment
Colour changed: repaint the visible bar and erase any excess
The simulator includes this colour-change exception
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Run the meter at 10 Hz
slides.lead: Read every IMU sample; redraw only every fifth sample.
points: 50 Hz acquisition ÷ 5 = 10 Hz nominal meter updates
Inspect link stats at the end
A repeated page name keeps reruns predictable
slides.code:
python lab9_3_display_basics.py --replay
# ws28p live instead:
python lab9_3_display_basics.py
slides.notes: Replay still opens a physical screen board. Ask which operation is saved when the integer width is unchanged and the colour is unchanged.

slides.title: Returning to a hidden page
slides.lead: Drawing for a page behind another tab can be dropped.
points: Use on_shown to repaint static content and reset chart state
Labs 9.4 and 9.5 install repaint callbacks
Lab 9.3 is simpler and does not install one: add it as an extension
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Display self-check
slides.lead: How large is a 100 × 50 RGB565 image?
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

options: 10,000 bytes; 20 strips of at most 512 bytes
quiz.explanation: 100×50×2=10,000 bytes. ceil(10,000/512)=20 payload strips; transport headers are extra.
